lines.text: Want sounds strong. Say would like!
Many learners say: I want a coffee, please.
Better: I would like a coffee, please.
I would like! I would like a coffee, please.

data.right: I would like a coffee, please.

native.tip: En español “quiero un café” es normal, pero en inglés “I want” suena brusco: mejor “I would like.”
native.caption: 🙈 Error común: “I want a coffee, please.” Para pedir con educación usa “I would like”: “I would like a coffee, please.” ¡Escucha a Carlos y repite! Practica más en la app Lexkite.
native.comment: Respuesta: “I would like”. En un café o tienda, “I would like” suena amable; “I want” suena brusco. Escribe una frase tuya con “I would like” o dila en voz alta: {link}

en.tip: “Quiero un café” is normal for learners, but “I want” sounds blunt in English: use “I would like.”
en.caption: Common mistake: “I want a coffee, please.” To ask politely use “I would like”: “I would like a coffee, please.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
